caption: The drawing is a technical blueprint of a piece of furniture labeled as a "Chest on Frame" from the Sewall House, Secretary, Maryland, intended for a bedroom, and part of the Brooklyn Museum collection. The drawing is rendered in thin, precise pencil or ink lines on a beige or yellowed background typical of aged paper. The drawing provides three views: a plan of the top and legs/stretchers at the top left, a front view at the bottom left, and an end view at the bottom right. The plan view shows the rectangular top surface of the chest, with the legs and stretchers indicated to the right of it. The front view displays two paneled upper doors with a geometric molding, a single row of two round drawer pulls below, and four turned legs joined at the base with horizontal stretchers, also turned. The end view shows the side panel, a single flat panel framed within, and the angled top edge. Dimension lines are included, indicating the widths and heights of specific parts, such as 28 1/2 inches for the front width and 17 1/4 inches for the end depth. In the upper right corner, a rectangular title box contains hand-written information about the object. A small linear scale marked in inches is also shown near the title box. The blueprint is monochromatic, using just the color of the paper and the gray or brown lines of the drawing medium. There are a few stains and signs of aging on the paper, such as brown spots, especially in the upper left and right corners.
title: Chest on Frame
